text:
nora: FYI rvl-legal bringup in staging: overall NDCG@10 +1.2% but MRR@5 for citation-style queries (e.g., 'Smith v. Jones, 1999 §12', '42 U.S.C. 1983') is down -6.0%. Need quick triage.

samir: wow that's large. paste slice table?

nora: quick paste from eval-run-legal-013:
```
metric            overall   citations_slice   faq_slice
NDCG@10           +1.2%     +0.9%             +1.5%
MRR@5             -0.1%     -6.0%             +0.4%
Top1_exact        -0.6pp    -7.8pp            -0.2pp
```
notes: new pipeline applied "normalize_punct=collapse" and stripped section symbols and citation parentheses during candidate dedupe. Also rolled int8 PTQ with asymmetric quant.

elaine: stripping § and parentheses for dedupe seems dangerous for legal citations. Exact-string anchors drive top1 for these queries. Could be the normalizer.

samir: Agreed. Another possibility: candidate dedupe merged separate cases that differ only by citation suffix, so the exact hit got merged into a broader doc with lower score.

eval-bot: Queued ablation: (A) normalizer=keep_symbols, (B) dedupe_strict=on (no merging if citations differ), (C) quant=fp16. Command: ./eval_rerank --model rvl-legal --dataset holdout_legal --slices citations --norm {keep,collapse} --dedupe {strict,merge} --quant {fp16,int8} ETA ~15m.

nora: also collect exact_phrase_match and merged_candidate_count metrics.

eval-bot: Job 8102 finished. Results (deltas vs rvl-legal baseline):
- A (norm=keep, dedupe=merge, quant=int8): citations MRR delta = +4.9% (partial recovery)
- B (norm=collapse, dedupe=strict, quant=int8): citations MRR delta = +5.5% (partial recovery)
- C (norm=keep, dedupe=strict, quant=fp16): citations MRR delta = +7.2% (near full recovery)
additional: exact_phrase_match for citations_slice recovered +6.9pp in C; merged_candidate_count fell 38% in B/C. int8 vs fp16 shows a small ~0.7pp penalty on top1 for this slice.

elaine: So primary drivers are normalizer stripping symbols and dedupe merging; quant is a minor amplifier. Good news: config fixes should solve this without model revert.

samir: Actionable: 1) revert citation symbol stripping for queries and candidates that match citation regex (e.g., "§|U\.S\.C\.|v\."), 2) set dedupe_strict for legal domain traffic or add citation-aware merge rules, 3) keep int8 but schedule a short per-slice calibration pass if A/B shows residual drift.

nora: I'll prepare a small rollout: 5% A/B with norm=keep_symbols + dedupe_strict for legal-scope routes (query classifier gating). Rollout doc: https://go/rollout/rvl-legal-citation-fix.

ops-bot: Rollout created by nora: rvl-legal-citation-fix (5% -> 25% -> 100%) safety window 4h. Dedicated rollout hold flagged.

eval-bot: Starting A/B; collecting exact_phrase_match/top1/mrr every 10m.

elaine: Also adding a unit test in the eval harness: sample citation queries must maintain exact_phrase_match >= 95% of baseline after any token/normalizer change. Will add to PR checklist.

samir: Good. Small note: we should log merged_candidate provenance so we can inspect whether merged docs differ by citation suffix; that'll help debugging future merges. Filing ticket.

nora: Thanks team. Learned: domain-specific punctuation (citations, section marks) are high-signal anchors and deserve explicit preserve rules before blanket normalizers. Will post A/B numbers here. :mag:
